editorial:
Imagine a man who has completely given up on life, spending his days drinking and ignoring the world around him. That is Pratap, a guy who seems lost until a brave journalist named Megha pushes him to wake up and fight back. You get a real sense of frustration as you watch him try to convince his own people to stand up for their rights against corrupt politicians and mean cops. It is a loud, angry, and emotional ride that feels like a classic battle between the little guy and the big system. The movie does not hold back on the drama, making you feel the heat of the streets and the desperation of the characters.

What really makes this work is the powerhouse acting, especially the shouting matches and the intense dialogues that stay with you. The action is old-school and punchy, though some parts might feel a bit slow or too dramatic for today's standards. If you love movies where a hero takes a stand against the world, you will love this. It is a great pick for a weekend binge with the family.
endingExplained: After fighting a long war against the corrupt system, Pratap realizes that violence alone cannot fix society. In the final showdown, he faces off against the villains in a bloody clash. While he manages to take down the bad guys and expose their crimes, the law eventually catches up with him. He accepts his fate and dies, but his death serves as a wake-up call, finally inspiring his community to stand up and fight for justice on their own.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic masala movies with a strong social message.
